title: Capstone: society, identity and the whole level
objectives: Discuss society and identity topics: the national language debate, OFW life, and social media
Read a long opinion feature and track its argument structure
Recycle and combine the whole level: voice choice, nominalization, irrealis, concession, formal register, idiom and debate moves
Self-assess readiness for the B2 exam

grammar.title: The wikang pambansa debate: vocabulary and fault lines
grammar.explanation:
No B2 speaker can dodge the language question, so learn its terms. Wikang pambansa 'national language' (Filipino); wikang opisyal 'official language' (Filipino and English); mga wikang panrehiyon 'regional languages' (Cebuano, Ilocano, Hiligaynon, at iba pa); katutubong wika 'indigenous language'. Key verbs: pangalagaan 'to safeguard', payabungin 'to make flourish', ipagmalaki 'to take pride in', mawalan ng gamit 'to fall out of use', maglaho 'to vanish'.

The fault lines, in the concessive frames you now command: Bagaman Filipino ang wikang pambansa, Ingles pa rin ang wika ng korte at ng negosyo. Iginigiit ng ilan na dapat palakasin ang Filipino sa agham at batas; iginigiit naman ng iba na kalamangan ng Pilipino ang Ingles sa pandaigdigang ekonomiya. Sa kabila nito, pumapanig ang marami sa multilinggwalismo: pangalagaan ang lahat.

Notice you are not learning new grammar here — you are aiming Unit 4's concession, Unit 8's attribution, and Unit 9's debate moves at one real controversy. That is what capstone means.

grammar.title: Talking about the OFW experience and the digital town plaza
grammar.explanation:
The OFW (overseas Filipino worker) story runs through modern Tagalog discourse and through this level's own readings — remittances (padala, Unit 1), separation, sacrifice. Core terms: mangibang-bansa 'to go abroad (to live/work)', sakripisyo, kalungkutan 'loneliness' (ka- -an!), pamilyang nagkakalayo 'families growing apart', bagong bayani 'modern-day hero' — the standard, and debated, epithet for OFWs. Frame sentences: Napilitan siyang mangibang-bansa upang matustusan ang pag-aaral ng mga anak — see Unit 5's upang and Unit 2's gerund working together.

Social media has its own register battleground. Discussion vocabulary: kalatnigan is not standard — use social media / mga social media platform as loanwords, plus: mag-post, mag-share, i-like (office-Taglish morphology, Unit 11), impormasyong mali o pekeng balita 'misinformation / fake news', maging viral 'to go viral', paninirang-puri 'defamation', kalayaan sa pagpapahayag 'freedom of expression' (ka- -an + pagpapahayag: two Unit 2 patterns stacked).

When you argue about these topics, the examiners are listening for the full toolkit: a claim, numbered reasons, one concession honestly granted, a counter, and a conclusion — delivered in the right register for the room.

grammar.title: Level review: the seven habits of a B2 speaker
grammar.explanation:
Before the exam, audit yourself against the level's spine. (1) Voice for flow: in any paragraph you produce, can you say WHY each verb is actor, object, locative or benefactive focus? (2) Nominalization: can you turn kung mahirap ang buhay into ang kahirapan ng buhay, and matapos siyang mamatay into pagkamatay niya? (3) Irrealis: sana + completed for regret, dapat sana for hindsight, kung hindi lang for the single obstacle, sakaling for the remote future. (4) Concession: kahit/bagaman inside the sentence, gayunpaman/sa kabila nito between sentences, samantalang for reproachful contrast.

(5) Cause and purpose: dahil sa → dulot ng → bunga ng as register rises; upang/para for purpose; and the ng/nang rule under pressure. (6) Register switching: the same request as a text to a friend, a spoken office line, and a formal letter sentence — three different sentences, one meaning. (7) Reading stamina: a 250-word editorial should now yield its main claim, its evidence, and its concessions on one careful pass.

Where you wobble, reread that unit. The exam does not test trivia; it tests whether these seven habits fire together at conversation speed.

dialogue.title: Video call mula Dubai
dialogue.context: OFW nurse Amelia video-calls her brother Danny in Batangas; the talk moves from remittances to the language her daughter is losing, pulling in the level's big themes.

lines.speaker: Danny
lines.tl: Ate, natanggap na namin ang padala mo. Sabi ni Inay, sobra na naman — dapat sana ay nag-ipon ka na lang para sa sarili mo.
lines.en: Ate, we received your remittance. Mother says it's too much again — you should have just saved it for yourself.

lines.speaker: Amelia
lines.tl: Hayaan mo na. Para sa matrikula ni Nica iyan at sa gamot ni Inay. Kung hindi lang dahil sa inyo, baka matagal na akong umuwi.
lines.en: Let it be. That's for Nica's tuition and Mother's medicine. If it weren't for all of you, I might have come home long ago.

lines.speaker: Danny
lines.tl: Alam mo, tinanong ako ni Nica kahapon kung bakit raw 'bagong bayani' ang tawag sa mga OFW. Ang hirap sagutin.
lines.en: You know, Nica asked me yesterday why OFWs are called 'modern-day heroes'. It was hard to answer.

lines.speaker: Danny
lines.tl: Sinabi kong dahil sa sakripisyo — na pinipili ninyong magtiis ng kalungkutan para matustusan ang pamilya. Pero inamin ko ring may mga nagsasabi na hindi dapat normal ang ganitong pagkakahiwalay.
lines.en: I said it's because of sacrifice — that you all choose to endure loneliness to support the family. But I also admitted some say this kind of separation shouldn't be normal.

lines.speaker: Amelia
lines.tl: Tama ang dalawang panig. Ipinagmamalaki kong nabubuhay ko kayo, pero itaga mo sa bato: pag nakatapos si Nica, uuwi na ako. Ayokong lumaki siyang parang bisita lang ako sa video call.
lines.en: Both sides are right. I'm proud I can provide for you, but mark my words: once Nica graduates, I'm coming home. I don't want her growing up with me as just a visitor on a video call.

lines.speaker: Danny
lines.tl: Sana nga. O siya, may isa pang balita: puro Ingles na si Nica sa bahay. Sabi ng titser, mahina raw siya sa Filipino.
lines.en: I hope so. Oh, one more piece of news: Nica speaks pure English at home now. Her teacher says she's weak in Filipino.

lines.speaker: Amelia
lines.tl: Naku. Hindi naman sa masama ang Ingles — kalamangan pa nga iyon. Pero kapag naglaho ang Tagalog sa dila ng anak ko, parang may naglaho ring bahagi ng pagkakakilanlan niya.
lines.en: Oh no. It's not that English is bad — it's even an advantage. But if Tagalog vanishes from my daughter's tongue, it feels like part of her identity vanishes too.

lines.speaker: Danny
lines.tl: Kaya nga sinisimulan ko na siyang kuwentuhan ng mga alamat tuwing gabi. Kagabi, ang Alamat ng Pinya — natawa siya sa isang libong mata.
lines.en: That's why I've started telling her legends at night. Last night, the Legend of the Pineapple — she laughed at the thousand eyes.

lines.speaker: Amelia
lines.tl: Mahusay! Sa susunod na uwi ko, dadalhan ko siya ng mga aklat na Filipino. At mag-uusap kami — sa Tagalog, kahit pautal-utal siya.
lines.en: Wonderful! On my next trip home, I'll bring her Filipino books. And we'll talk — in Tagalog, even if she stumbles.

lines.speaker: Danny
lines.tl: Sa kabuuan, ate, ang layo mo man, ikaw pa rin ang gumagawa ng paraan para buo ang pamilyang ito.
lines.en: All in all, ate, however far away you are, you're still the one finding ways to keep this family whole.

lines.speaker: Amelia
lines.tl: Bayanihan din iyan, Danny — kahit ang bahay na binubuhat natin ay nasa dalawang bansa.
lines.en: That's bayanihan too, Danny — even if the house we're carrying stands in two countries.

reading.title: Sanaysay: Ang wika sa panahon ng scroll
reading.tl:
May katanungang paulit-ulit na itinatanong sa akin ng aking mga estudyante: "Sir, bakit pa po kami mag-aaral ng Filipino, e Ingles naman ang wika ng trabaho at ng internet?" Isang tapat na tanong, at karapat-dapat sa tapat na sagot.

Una, hindi totoo na walang halaga ang Filipino sa ekonomiya. Ang call center na nagsisilbi sa mga kababayan, ang nars na umaaruga sa pasyenteng Pilipino, ang abogadong nagpapaliwanag ng batas sa isang magsasaka — lahat sila ay nangangailangan ng wikang naiintindihan ng kanilang kausap. Ang wika ay hindi lamang kasangkapan ng kalakalan; kasangkapan ito ng katarungan at ng kalusugan.

Ikalawa, aminado ako: makapangyarihan ang Ingles, at kalamangan ng Pilipino ang kahusayan dito. Hindi ko iyon binabalewala. Ngunit ang kakayahan sa dalawang wika ay hindi tulad ng isang tasa ng tubig na kapag ibinuhos mo sa isa ay mawawalan ang isa. Ayon sa mga pag-aaral, ang batang matatas sa sariling wika ay mas mabilis ding matuto ng pangalawa.

Ikatlo — at dito ako pumapanig — ang wika ay pagkakakilanlan. Sa social media, nagbabasa tayo ng libu-libong salita araw-araw, ngunit ilan dito ang salitang nagmula sa ating mga lola, alamat, at awitin? Kapag naglaho ang mga iyon sa ating dila, may naglalahong bahagi rin ng ating pagkatao.

Samakatuwid, hindi ko sinasabing talikuran ang Ingles. Ang sinasabi ko: huwag nating ipagpalit ang isang kayamanan sa isa pa, gayong kaya nating angkinin ang dalawa. Ang tunay na tanong ay hindi kung aling wika ang pipiliin natin, kundi kung anong klaseng Pilipino ang nais nating maging.
reading.en:
There is a question my students ask me again and again: "Sir, why should we still study Filipino, when English is the language of work and of the internet?" An honest question, deserving an honest answer.

First, it is not true that Filipino has no economic value. The call center that serves our countrymen, the nurse caring for a Filipino patient, the lawyer explaining the law to a farmer — all of them need a language their listener understands. Language is not only an instrument of commerce; it is an instrument of justice and of health.

Second, I admit it: English is powerful, and Filipinos' skill in it is an advantage. I do not dismiss that. But ability in two languages is not like a cup of water that empties one side when you pour it into the other. According to studies, a child fluent in their own language learns a second one faster too.

Third — and here is where I take my stand — language is identity. On social media we read thousands of words every day, but how many of them are words that came from our grandmothers, from our legends, from our songs? When those vanish from our tongues, a part of our selfhood vanishes as well.

Therefore, I am not saying we should turn our backs on English. What I am saying is: let us not trade one treasure for another, when we are capable of owning both. The real question is not which language we will choose, but what kind of Filipino we wish to become.

exercises.prompt: Why are OFWs commonly called 'mga bagong bayani'?
choices: They fought in historical revolutions.
Their sacrifice and remittances sustain families and the economy.
They are all nurses by profession.
They star in action films abroad.
exercises.explain: Bagong bayani 'modern-day heroes' honors OFWs' sacrifice — enduring separation and sending remittances that support families and the national economy. The label itself is debated, as the unit discusses.

exercises.prompt: Tungkulin nating ___ ang mga katutubong wika bago tuluyang maglaho. (safeguard)
exercises.hint: the -an verb of care from this unit
exercises.explain: Pangalagaan 'to safeguard/care for' takes the languages as its focus; maglaho 'to vanish' names the danger.

exercises.prompt: Pinadalhan niya ng pera ang kanyang mga magulang. Which Unit 1 pattern is at work?
choices: i- theme focus: the money is the ang-phrase
-an recipient focus: the parents are the ang-phrase
actor focus: siya is the ang-phrase
locative focus on the bank
exercises.explain: Padalhan is the -an (recipient-focus) counterpart of magpadala: the parents receive the focus, the money is the ng-phrase — exactly the ibigay/bigyan logic from Unit 1.

exercises.prompt: Pinalalala ng pekeng balita ang ___ ng lipunan; pagkakaisa ang kailangan natin. (disunity)
exercises.explain: Pagkakawatak-watak 'fragmentation, disunity' contrasts with pagkakaisa 'unity' — both built with the ka- family of abstractions from Unit 2.

exercises.prompt: From the essay: what is the author's answer to 'why still study Filipino'?
choices: Because English will soon disappear from the Philippines.
Because Filipino serves justice, bilinguals learn better, and language carries identity.
Because the law requires it and nothing more.
Because social media is written mostly in Filipino.
exercises.explain: The essay's three numbered points: Filipino has real economic and civic value (justice, health), bilingualism strengthens rather than weakens learning, and language is identity.

exercises.prompt: The essay concedes 'makapangyarihan ang Ingles, at kalamangan... ang kahusayan dito' — then counters with the cup-of-water image. Which unit's move is this, aimed at which claim?
choices: Unit 4's concede-then-counter, against the idea that learning Filipino costs you English
Unit 3's counterfactual, against the history of English in schools
Unit 6's formal complaint, against the Department of Education
Unit 7's euphemism, against direct speech
exercises.explain: Aminado ako grants English's power (concession); ngunit + the cup metaphor rejects the zero-sum premise (counter) — the Unit 4/9 move in essay form.

exercises.tl: Napilitan siyang mangibang-bansa upang matustusan ang pag-aaral ng kanyang mga anak, kahit alam niyang matinding kalungkutan ang kapalit.
choices: She was forced to go abroad to fund her children's schooling, even knowing the price was intense loneliness.
She refused to go abroad because her children were lonely.
She went abroad to study, leaving her children with relatives.
Her children went abroad while she stayed home, lonely.
exercises.explain: Napilitang mangibang-bansa = 'was forced to go abroad'; upang matustusan gives the purpose; kahit + kalungkutan ang kapalit concedes the cost. Units 3, 4, 5 and 12 vocabulary in one sentence.

exercises.prompt: Kung hindi lang dahil sa mga padala ng aking ate, hindi sana ako nakapagtapos ng kolehiyo.
exercises.answer: If it weren't for my older sister's remittances, I would not have finished college.
accept: If it weren't for my older sister's remittances, I would not have finished college
If not for my big sister's remittances, I wouldn't have been able to graduate from college
Were it not for my sister's remittances, I would not have graduated from college
exercises.explain: Kung hindi lang dahil sa X names the decisive factor (Unit 3); hindi sana nakapagtapos is the unreal outcome with the abilitative naka-.

exercises.prompt: Although social media connects us, it also spreads fake news faster than the truth.
exercises.answer: Bagaman nagdurugtong sa atin ang social media, mas mabilis din nitong ikinakalat ang pekeng balita kaysa sa katotohanan.
accept: Bagaman nagdurugtong sa atin ang social media, mas mabilis din nitong ikinakalat ang pekeng balita kaysa sa katotohanan
Kahit nagdurugtong sa atin ang social media, mas mabilis din nitong ikinakalat ang pekeng balita kaysa sa totoo
Bagaman pinagdurugtong tayo ng social media, mas mabilis din nitong ikinakalat ang pekeng balita kaysa sa katotohanan
exercises.explain: Bagaman (Unit 4) concedes the benefit; the counter uses ikalat (i- object focus) with fake news in focus and katotohanan (Unit 2 ka- -an) as the standard of comparison.

exercises.prompt: Register check (Units 6 and 11): which version of 'please send the report before Friday' belongs in a formal letter?
choices: I-send mo na 'yung report bago Biyernes ha.
Pakisend ng report bago Biyernes.
Hinihiling po naming maipadala ang ulat bago sumapit ang Biyernes.
Report! Biyernes! Bilis!
exercises.explain: The formal letter version uses hinihiling po naming + abilitative maipadala + the formal ulat and bago sumapit. The others are office Taglish, a casual paki- request, and shouting.

exercises.tl: Buhay pa rin ang diwa ng bayanihan: nag-ambagan ang buong barangay para maipaayos ang bahay ng mag-anak na nasunugan.
choices: The whole barangay pooled contributions to have the fire-stricken family's house repaired.
The barangay held a festival to celebrate a new house.
A family donated a house to the barangay after a fire.
The barangay demolished an unsafe house after a fire.
exercises.explain: Nag-ambagan = 'contributed jointly'; maipaayos = 'to have repaired' (causative pa- inside abilitative mai-); nasunugan = 'suffered a fire'. Bayanihan in action.

exercises.prompt: In my opinion, we should take pride in our own language; nevertheless, we should not turn our backs on English.
exercises.answer: Sa aking palagay, dapat nating ipagmalaki ang ating sariling wika; gayunpaman, hindi natin dapat talikuran ang Ingles.
accept: Sa aking palagay, dapat nating ipagmalaki ang ating sariling wika; gayunpaman, hindi natin dapat talikuran ang Ingles
Sa palagay ko, dapat nating ipagmalaki ang sarili nating wika. Gayunpaman, hindi natin dapat talikuran ang Ingles
Sa aking palagay, dapat nating ipagmalaki ang ating wika; gayunpaman, huwag nating talikuran ang Ingles
exercises.explain: Sa aking palagay stakes the claim (Unit 9); ipagmalaki carries the pride; gayunpaman (Unit 4) pivots to the balancing point — the whole level in one sentence.
